questions.question: Which of the following former Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh passed away in October 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Mulayam Singh Yadav'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Samajwadi Party(SP) founder and three-time Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister, Mulayam Singh Yadav passed away at Medanta Hospital in Gurugram on October 10.
 
• He was 82. The SP patriarch’s condition had been “quite critical” for the past few weeks and he was on life-saving drugs.
 
• Though he had been away from active politics for a while, with his son Akhilesh leading the party since 2017, he was counted among the prominent opposition forces in the country. For the Samajwadi Party, he remained "Neta-ji" - a term that even his son used for him.
 
• One of Uttar Pradesh's top politicians, Mulayam Singh was also Union Defence Minister in 1996-98.
 
• Mulayam Singh first became an MLA in 1967. During his second term as MLA, then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi declared the Emergency and Mulayam Singh, like many opposition leaders, went to jail.
 
• Mulayam Singh was elected 10 times as an MLA and seven times as Lok Sabha MP.
 
• A former wrestler, Mulayam Singh was known to be an astute politician who didn't flinch when it came to striking deals, even with bitter rivals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narayan Dutt Tiwari,** the former Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, passed away in October 2018. 

 
 
• He was also the Chief Minister of Uttarakhand and served as a Union Minister in the Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Kalyan Singh, **another former Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, passed away in August 2021.
 
 
• He was also a Governor of Rajasthan and served as a Union Minister in the Government of India.-
 
 
 
• **Vijay Kashyap **is not a former Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh.
 
 
• It is unclear who this person is, as there are multiple people with this name.

questions.question: Which of the following is a metamorphic rock?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Quartzite.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Quarzite is a metamorphic rock formed from pure quartz sandstone.
 
• It is white to grey in color.
 
• Orthoquartzite is a very pure quartz sandstone composed of usually well-rounded quartz grains cemented by Silica.
 
• Orthoquartzite is often 99% SiO2 with only very minor amounts of iron oxide and trace-resistant minerals such as zircon, rutile, and magnetite.
 
• Quartzite is very resistant to chemical weathering and often forms ridges and resistant hilltop​rns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
 

 Types of rocks
 Characteristics
 
 

 Igneous rock
 
 
 
• It is formed when molten rock (magma or lava) cools and solidifies.
 
• Igneous rock may form with or without crystallization.
 
• It may be intrusive (plutonic) rocks or extrusive (volcanic) rocks.
 
• For example, Granite, Basalt, etc.
 
 
 
 

 Sedimentary rock
 
 
 
• They originate when particles settle out of water or air, or by precipitation of minerals from water.
 
• They accumulate in layers.
 
• For example, Sandstone, Limestone, etc.
 
 
 
 

 Metamorphic rock
 
 
 
• They formed when existing rocks are changed by heat, pressure, or reactive fluids, such as hot, mineral-laden water.
 
• For example, Marble, Quartzite, Schist, etc.

questions.question: Which among the following Bihu is also known as Rongali Bihu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Bohag Bihu__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bohag Bihu, also known as the Rongali Bihu, is a joyous festival that marks the start of spring and the Assamese New Year.
 
• Assam celebrates Bihu, Baishagu, Ali-Ai-Ligang, Baikho, Rongker, and Rajini Gabra as its important holidays. Bohaggiyo Bishu, Jonbill Mela, Ambubashi Mela, and others include Harni Gabra.
 
• The most well-known Bihu, Bohag Bihu (mid-April; also known as Rongali Bihu), marks the beginning of the Assamese New Year (about 14–15 April) and the arrival of spring.
 
• On April 14th of every year, the Indian state of Assam observes a regional public holiday known as Bohag Bihu.
 
• Depending on the day of the week it falls on, a number of days of public holidays may be announced, and occasionally it is also a public holiday in the neighbouring state of Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• This national holiday, also known as Rongali Bihu, is celebrated in Assam, one of India's most picturesque states noted for its tea gardens, verdant forests, and the Brahmaputra River.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• "Garu Bihu" is the name given to the first day of the Bihu.
 
• On this day, folks bathe and pray for the health and safety of their home cattle while they take them to the river for a bath.
 
• People take a turmeric-based bath on "Manuh Bihu," the second day of Bihu.
 
• Families eat a variety of larus or laddus and pithas, or rice cakes.
 
• People visit neighbours and family members during Bihu celebrations to say hello to one another and show their respect for the family's elders by giving them a fresh "Gamosa" (a traditional Assamese hand-woven cotton towel with red designs with a white background).
 
• Ali-ai-ligang:
 
 
• ​The Mising or Mishing tribal people of Assam and other Northeast Indian states celebrate Ali-Aye-Ligang or Ali-Ai-Ligang, a spring festival related with agriculture, on the occasion of the start of the Ahu paddy cultivation.
 
• The celebration signifies the beginning of seeding.
 
• Three words make up the festival's name: "Ali" (legumes), "Aye" (seed), and "Ligang" (sow).
 
• On the first Wednesday of Phalguna, the 12th month of the Hindu calendar, the festival gets underway.
 
 
 
• Me-Dum-Me-Phi: 
 
 
• ​Mae Dam Mae Phi is a significant event that the Tai-Ahom have celebrated since very early times.
 
• "Me" is an offering word. Both "Dam" and "Phi" refer to the gods.
 
• Hence, "Mae Dam Mae Phi" refers to sacrifices made to the spirits of the ancestors.
 
 
 
• Kati Bihu:
 
 
• ​On the first day of the Assamese calendar's "Kati" month, which often falls in the middle of October, Kati Bihu is observed. It falls on October 18 this year.
 
• The celebration heralds the shifting of the rice crop and the start of the season of new harvest.
 
• An observation of service, penance, and the desire for a better future, Kati Bihu.
 
• Despite the fact that each Assamese tribe has its own customs and celebrations of the day, the event is observed throughout the entire state of Assam.
 
• Outside the houses, lamps are lit, and a bamboo path is built as a trail for the ancesto

questions.question: The _______ provides for measures to deter fugitive economic offenders from evading the process of law in India by staying outside the jurisdiction of Indian courts.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018:-

 
 
• An Act to provide for measures to deter fugitive economic offenders from evading the process of law in India by staying outside the jurisdiction of Indian courts, to preserve the sanctity of the rule of law in India, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. 
 
• An FEO is defined by The Fugitive Economic Offenders (FEO) Act, 2018 as “any individual against whom a warrant for arrest in relation to a scheduled offence has been issued by any court in India, who
 
 
• (i) has left India so as to avoid criminal prosecution; or
 
• (ii) abroad refusing to return to India to face criminal prosecution”.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Economic Offenders Act, 2018 **is an incorrect option as there is no such act. The correct name of the act is the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018.
 
• **Fugitive Offenders Act, 2015** is an incorrect option as it is a Hong Kong law that allows the extradition of fugitives to mainland China, which has faced criticism for violating human rights.
 
• **Foreign Economic Offenders Act, 2018** is an incorrect option as there is no such act.

questions.question: Sultan Johor Cup is associated with which sport?
questions.solution:

questions.question: Which of the following is a fundamental duty?

options.text: To renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of men
To renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of any administrative officials
To renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of advocates
To renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** To renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women. **__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of Fundamental Duties was borrowed by India from the USSR.
 
• The inclusion of Fundamental Duties brought our Constitution in line with Article 29 (1) of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and with provisions in several modern Constitutions of other countries.
 
• The duties enumerated in Article 51A of the Constitution are unique to the Indian ethos and value systems.
 
• However, the concept of fundamental duties is also seen in the constitutions of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam enjoins that “the public property of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam is sacred and inviolable.
 
• The fundamental duties require all citizens to respect the national symbols of India, the constitution, its heritage and to preserve its culture and assist in the defense.
 
• The duties mandate the spirit of brotherhood, protect public property, and the environment, avoid violence and strive towards excellence in all spheres of life.
 
• In case of violation of fundamental duties, it is held in contempt of the constitution and is punishable under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971.
 
• The list of 11 Fundamental Duties under article 51-A to be obeyed by every Indian citizen is given below:__

 
• Abide by the Indian Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem
 
• Cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom
 
• Uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India
 
• Defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so
 
• **Promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities and to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women**
 
• Value and preserve the rich heritage of the country’s composite culture
 
• Protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures
 
• Develop scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform
 
• Safeguard public property and to abjure violence 
 
• Strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement
 
• Provide opportunities for education to one's child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years. This duty was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/292e0c96dd6c006ce1f3ef21b86308c7c73a2bc69f508d641b46f352d114f429.png] __Important Points__

 
• **The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added 10 Fundamental Duties to the Indian Constitution.**
 
• **86th Amendment Act 2002 later added 11th Fundamental Duty to the list.\**
 
• Swaran Singh Committee in 1976 recommended Fundamental Duties, the necessity of which was felt during the internal emergency of 1975-77.

questions.question: Harshavardhana tried to cross the Narmada to march into the Deccan, but was stopped by a ruler belonging to the Chalukya dynasty, ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ Pulakeshin II.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• Pulakeshin II, the King of the Chalukya dynasty defeated Harshavardhana when he seeks to enlarge his Empire into the southern peninsula of India.
 
• He defeated Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada river in 618 AD.
 
• The Aihole inscription was written by Ravikirti, court poet of Chalukya King Pulakesin II who reigned from 610 to 642 CE.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya:**__

 
 
• Chandragupta Maurya was the founder of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• He, at the young age of 25, captured Pataliputra from the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty, Dhanananda.
 
• In this task, he was assisted by Kautilya, who was also known as Chanakya or Vishnugupta.
 
 
 
• Samudragupta 
 
 
• He was the first significant ruler of the Gupta Dynasty.
 
• Having come to the throne, he decided to extend the boundaries of his empire to cover the multiple kingdoms and republics that existed outside its pale.
 
• Known as the Napoleon of India for his conquests, he was also a man of many talents and laid a firm foundation for the empire.

questions.question: Net Worth = Assets - _______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Net Worth = Assets - Liabilities__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The book value of the equity held by shareholders of a corporation is referred to as "Net worth."
 
• It can also be thought of as the net worth of a corporation that its shareholders would be able to claim in the event that all of its assets were liquidated and all of its obligations were paid off.
 
• To put it another way, it is the sum of assets that remain after all liabilities have been settled.
 
• Stockholder's equity and shareholder's equity are other names for a company's net worth.
 
• By deducting the subject company's total liabilities from its total assets, one can arrive at the formula for net worth. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/292e0c96dd6c006ce1f3ef21b86308c7c73a2bc69f508d641b46f352d114f429.png] Important Points__

__
 
• Although equity and net worth are sometimes used interchangeably, they are occasionally employed in different circumstances.
 
• The net worth calculation takes into account both assets and liabilities.
 
• The following are the two things to keep in mind when thinking about net worth:
 
 
• If net worth is more than zero, it can pay off debt and has strong financial growth.
 
• If net worth is zero, the company cannot pay its debts and has negative financial growth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Assets **are the resources owned by an individual or a company that has monetary value and** can be used to generate income or provide future benefits.**
 
• ** Liabilities **can be short-term or long-term and include loans, mortgages, accounts payable, etc.
 
• **Equity **can be in the form of common stock, preferred stock, retained earnings, etc.
 
• Net worth is an important indicator of the financial health and stability of an individual or a company.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the first elected Parliament come into existence?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __1952__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the year 1952, the first Elected Parliament with two houses came into being in India.

 
 
• The first general elections under the new Constitution were held during the year 1951-52.
 
• The first elected Parliament came into existence in April 1952.
 
• The Seventeenth Lok Sabha was held in May 2019.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• Indian Parliament is the supreme legislative body of India.
 
• The Indian Parliament comprises of the President and the two Houses -
 
 
• Rajya Sabha 
 
• Lok Sabha 
 
 
 
• Lok Sabha:
 
 
• 543 members are directly elected by citizens of India on the basis of a universal adult franchise representing Parliamentary constituencies across the country.
 
• It has a term of five years.
 
 
 
• Rajya Sabha:
 
 
• Rajya Sabha or the upper house is a permanent body not subject to dissolution.
 
• One-third of the members retire every second year and are replaced by newly elected members.
 
• Each member is elected for a term of six years.
 
 
 
• Session of Parliament :
 
 
• The period during which the House meets to conduct its business is called a session.
 
• The Constitution empowers the President to summon each House at such intervals that there should not be more than a six-month gap between the two sessions. 
 
 
 
• The President has the power to summon and prorogue either House of Parliament or to dissolve Lok Sabha.
 
• The Constitution of India came into force on January 26, 1950.

questions.question: Which are the two social groups in India which are most vulnerable to poverty?

options.text: Scheduled tribes and Other Backward Classes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Scheduled tribes and Scheduled castes.**__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• The social groups most vulnerable to poverty are the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribe households.
 
• Both of these groups have above-average levels of poverty indicators in the rural and the urban population.
 
• 51 out of 100 people belonging to scheduled tribes are not able to meet their basic needs.
 
• Similarly, 50% of casual workers in urban areas are below the poverty line.
 
• About 50% of landless agricultural workers and 43% of scheduled castes are also poor. 
 
• Women, elderly people, and female infants are the poorest of the poor because they are denied equal access to resources available to the family.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

__
 
• Several provisions have been incorporated in the Constitution for safeguarding and promoting the interests and rights of the Scheduled Tribes.
 
• Article 46
 
 
• The state shall promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker section
 
• Protect them from social injustice and all forms of exploitation.
 
 
 
• Article 23
 
 
• Prohibits traffic in human beings, beggars, forced labor has a special significance for Scheduled Tribes.
 
 
 
• Article 243D provides reservation of Seats for Scheduled Tribes in Panchayats. 
 
• Article 330 provides reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in the House of the People.
 
• Article 332 provides reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in Legislative Assemblies of the States.
 
• Article 334 provides the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and the State Vidhan Sabha

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__ **

 
• ** Forward castes** and Brahmins are generally considered to be among the most privileged and affluent social groups in India. While there may be individual cases of poverty within these groups, they do not face the same systemic barriers and discrimination as Scheduled tribes and Scheduled castes.
 
• **Scheduled tribes and Other Backward Classes (OBCs)** are both marginalized social groups in India. However, OBCs are generally considered to be less vulnerable to poverty than Scheduled tribes, as they have greater access to education and employment opportunities.
 
• **Brahmins are traditionally considered to be a high-caste social group**, while Scheduled castes are traditionally considered to be a low-caste social group. While poverty rates may be higher among Scheduled castes, Brahmins as a group do not face the same systemic barriers and discrimination as Scheduled castes.

questions.question: The _______ of a country is measured by the development of manufacturing industries.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** economic strength.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The economic strength of a country is measured by the development of manufacturing industries because it contributes to the country's GDP and provides employment opportunities to the people.**
 
• Manufacturing industries also help in the growth of other sectors such as **transportation, communication, and services.**
 
• Debt, expenditure, and liability are not measures of** economic strength but rather financial obligations or expenses that a country incurs.**
 
• Debt is the amount of money a country owes to** lenders, expenditure is the amount of money spent on goods and services, and liability is the financial obligations of a country.**
 
• While these factors are important for a country's financial health, they do not directly contribute to its economic strength.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** **** Debt:** It is the amount of money a country owes to lenders, both domestic and foreign. 

 
 
• It can be used to finance government spending, but too much debt can lead to financial instability and can negatively affect a country's credit rating.
 
 
 
• ** Expenditure: I**t refers to the amount of money a country spends on goods and services, both for consumption and investment purposes.
 
 
• It includes both government and private spending.
 
 
 
• ** Liability: **It refers to the financial obligations of a country, including both short-term and long-term debt, as well as future obligations such as pensions and other entitlements.
 
 
• It is an important measure of a country's financial health as it indicates its ability to meet its financial obligations.

questions.question: How is quicklime produced?

options.text: By double decomposition of calcium oxide and water
By displacement of calcium oxide and calcium carbonate
By decomposition of calcium carbonate into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide on heating.
By decomposition of calcium carbonate and calcium hydroxide

questions.solution:
__Explanation:__

__
 
• Calcium oxide, commonly known as lime, is a chemical compound with the formula CaO.
 
• Calcium oxide, also known as quicklime. It is believed that quicklime is one of the oldest chemicals known to mankind. It can also be called quicklime or lime.
 
• Calcium oxide can be produced by the thermal decomposition of materials such as limestone or shell that contain calcium carbonate (CaCO3 mineral calcite) in a lime kiln.
 
• The process used to prepare quicklime is called calcination. It is a process that begins with the thermal decomposition of the reactants at high temperatures but ensures that the temperature is kept well below the melting point.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• **Sodium Bicarbonate:**

 
 
• Sodium bicarbonate, also known as baking soda, is primarily used in baking as a leavening agent.
 
• It reacts with the acidic components in the solution, releasing carbon dioxide, which causes the solution to expand and creates the characteristic texture in pancakes, cakes, quick breads, soda breads, and other baked and fried foods.
 
 
 
• **Calcium Carbonate​:**
 
 
• It is an inorganic chemical compound whose chemical formula is CaCO₃.
 
• Calcium carbonate is a non-toxic and odorless compound commonly found as a white mineral that occurs naturally in chalk, limestone, and stone.
 
 
 
• **Silicon Dioxide**:
 
 
• SiO₂ is an oxide of silicon whose chemical name is silicon dioxide.
 
• It is also called silica or silicic oxide or silicic acid.
 
• It is found widely in nature in the form of quartz.

questions.question: Which currency notes were demonetised by the government of India in 2016?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹500 and ₹1,000**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• On 8 November 2016, the government of India announced the demonetization of all Rs. 500 and Rs. 1000 notes of the Mahatma Gandhi Series.
 
• This announcement also included the issuance of new Rs. 500 and Rs. 2000 banknotes in exchange for old notes.
 
• Due to the demonetization drive, there is a considerable increase in the number of Income Tax Returns (ITRs) filed.
 
• Objectives of Demonetisation:
 
 
• To discourage the use of high-denomination notes for illegal transactions and thus curb the widespread use of black money.
 
• To encourage the digitization of commercial transactions, formalize the economy and so, and boost government tax revenues.
 
 
 
• Operation Clean Money:
 
 
• It was launched by the Income Tax Department (CBDT) for the e-verification of large cash deposits made during the period from 9th November to 30th December 2016.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/292e0c96dd6c006ce1f3ef21b86308c7c73a2bc69f508d641b46f352d114f429.png] Important Points__

 History of Demonetization -

 
• In 1946, the currency notes of Rs 1,000 and Rs 10,000 were removed from circulation.
 
• In 1978, Prime Minister of India Morarji Desai announced the currency ban taking Rs 1000, Rs 5000 and Rs 10,000 out of circulation.

questions.question: He is perhaps best known for his speech at the Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago in 1893. Who is 'he' referred to?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Swami Vivekananda__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Swami Vivekananda

 
 
• Swami Vivekananda (1863–1902) is best known in the United States for his groundbreaking speech to the 1893 World's Parliament of Religions in which he introduced Hinduism to America and called for religious tolerance and an end to fanaticism.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

__
 
• Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramkrishna Mission at Belur in Howrah in 1897. It is a social service and charitable society.
 
• The objectives of this Mission are providing humanitarian relief and social work through the establishment of schools, colleges, hospitals, and orphanages.
 
• He asked the people to improve the lives of the poor and depressed classes. He believed that service to mankind is service to God.
 
• The original name of Swami Vivekananda was Narendranath Dutta (1863-1902). 
 
• He became the most famous disciple of Shri Ramkrishna Paramahamsa.
 
• In 1886, Narendranath took the vow of Sanyasa and was given the name, Vivekananda.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• ** Keshab Chandra Sen **was a Bengali Hindu philosopher and social reformer who founded the Brahmo Samaj, a socio-religious reform movement.
 
• **Swami Dayanand Saraswati **was the founder of the Arya Samaj, a Hindu reform movement.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi,** on the other hand, was a political leader and freedom fighter who led India to independence from British rule.
